title: Put both AED pads on a manikin's bare chest in the anterolateral position
instruction: Put the two AED training pads on the manikin's bare chest in the standard anterolateral position: one on the manikin's upper right chest just below the collarbone, beside the breastbone, and the other on the left side of its chest below the armpit. The pads must not touch. Then let go of them.
context: Emergency medical technicians and paramedics (O*NET 29-2042.00, 29-2043.00), firefighters (33-2011.00), nurses and trained lay rescuers put AED pads in the anterolateral position of the AHA and ERC resuscitation guidelines: one on the upper right chest below the collarbone, right of the breastbone; the other on the left side of the chest below the armpit, on the mid-axillary line about level with the V6 ECG electrode, so that the shock passes through the heart. Pads that touch can shunt the current across the skin. Studies of rescuers' placement find the side pad is often put too far forward, on the front of the chest under the nipple, and a rescuer facing the patient from the feet must remember that the patient's right is on the rescuer's left. The positions are found from landmarks on the body, not from marks.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Training torso: an armless adult manikin torso lying on its back with its head away from the arms, so the manikin's right side is toward +y (the left arm's side); a fixed flat-topped tan PLA shell 320 mm (along x) by 380 mm and 60 mm tall, from x 15.0 to 47.0 cm and y -19.0 to +19.0 cm. Its top is the bare chest; its edge at x 47.0 cm is the shoulder line. (2) Neck and head: fixed tan PLA parts past the shoulder line, a neck 20 x 100 x 50 mm tall from x 47.0 to 49.0 cm, centred on y 0, and the head, an upright cylinder 150 mm across and 90 mm tall centred at x 56.6 cm, y 0. (3) Landmarks: dark brown marks 1 mm thick (tape or paint) on the chest: the sternal notch, a 20 x 20 mm square centred at x 45.5 cm, y 0; the breastbone, a 120 x 10 mm line along the midline from x 32.5 to 44.5 cm; the two collarbones, 8 x 120 mm lines along the shoulder line centred at x 45.5 cm, from y +1.5 to +13.5 cm and from y -1.5 to -13.5 cm; the nipples, two discs 15 mm across centred at x 34.0 cm, y +8.5 cm and y -8.5 cm. (4) AED unit: a fixed yellow-green plastic box, 100 x 140 x 60 mm tall, centred at x 8.0 cm, y 0, between the arm bases (it only shows the setting; no cables are modelled). (5) Two AED training pads: identical loose white blocks, 110 x 70 x 18 mm, 40 g each: a training pad trimmed to 110 x 70 mm and glued to white closed-cell foam, 18 mm thick in all; either large face may end down. They lie flat on the table beside the torso: one centred at x 20.0 cm, y +27.0 cm with its long side along y, the other centred at x 20.0 cm, y -27.0 cm with its long side along x. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, measured with a tape from the torso's edges or read from a top photo; in simulation on the last step. A pad's position is its centre seen from above. Two positions: sternal, at x 40.0 cm, y +8.0 cm (the manikin's upper right chest: 70 mm below the shoulder line, 80 mm right of the breastbone line, below the collarbone and above the nipple line) and apical, at x 30.0 cm, y -14.5 cm (its left side below the armpit: 170 mm below the shoulder line, 145 mm left of the midline, 45 mm in from the chest's left edge, 40 mm below and 60 mm outside the left nipple). They are 246 mm apart, so a pad can earn credit at one of them only. A pad 'lies on the chest' when its centre is over the torso's top, it is tilted at most 10 degrees (either large face down) and its lowest point is within 5 mm of the chest top. It 'counts' when it lies on the chest and both grippers are clear of it: each gripper's finger zone at least 10 mm from the pad. A finger zone is every point within a radius of the 38 mm segment from the point between the gripper's finger tips back up the gripper, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the finger gap plus the 8 mm finger thickness, and half the fingers' 27 mm width across; 57 mm fully open). For the upright grippers this means the point between a gripper's finger tips at least 67 mm from the pad when fully open, 26 mm when closed. Score 0 if the two pads' outlines seen from above are less than 10 mm apart (touching, overlapping or one on the other). Otherwise each position earns 0.5 if a pad that counts has its centre within 25 mm of it, 0.25 if within 40 mm, 0 otherwise, and the score is the sternal credit plus the apical credit. The pads are identical: either may go in either position, in any heading, either face down. Possible scores: 0; 0.25 (one pad 25-40 mm off a position, nothing at the other); 0.5 (one pad within 25 mm and nothing at the other, or each pad 25-40 mm off its position); 0.75 (one within 25 mm, the other 25-40 mm off); 1.0 (both within 25 mm). A pad still held, on the table, standing on an edge, or more than 40 mm from both positions earns nothing: the mirror-image placement (the manikin's upper left chest and right side) scores 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with both pads still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, both pads are taken as clear of them.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The torso is a fixed flat-topped box: a real chest is curved and the apical pad wraps round its side, here it lies on the top 45 mm from the edge. The pads are stiff 18 mm blocks, smaller than most adult pads so a gripper spans one, with no adhesive, gel side or lead wires, so either face may be down. The scorer reads each gripper's finger-tip point, tool point and opening, not its heading, so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Put the two pads back flat on the table: one centred at x 20.0 cm, y +27.0 cm with its long side along y, the other at x 20.0 cm, y -27.0 cm with its long side along x. Nothing is consumed (training pads are reusable; real AED pads are single-use adhesive electrodes).
